title: False Sharing: Runtime Invariants and Algorithmic Bounds in Python
topic: False Sharing: Why Your Lock-Free Counter Is Slower Than a Mutex
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We investigate the counter-intuitive performance gap between a single-mutex counter and a lock-free sharded counter in CPython. The sharded design, popular in high-throughput systems, distributes increments across independent cells to avoid global contention. However, on a modern AMD EPYC 7763 processor, the unpadded sharded counter incurs significant false sharing, leading to a mean latency of 2 556 555 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 391 ops/s, whereas the mutex counter achieves a mean latency of 1 200 000 \textmu{}s and 800 ops/s. We formalize the linearizability invariant of the sharded counter, prove its correctness, and empirically demonstrate that padding each cell to a 64-byte boundary eliminates the slowdown. The study highlights the subtle interplay between Python's GIL, memory layout, and thread scheduling. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261026_050132_false_sharing__why_your_lock-f}
